newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean politicians slam intelligence services.
newsitem.headline: Chilean politicians slam intelligence services.

text.p: Chilean politicians attacked on Wednesday the country's intelligence services after four leftist guerrillas made a daring prison escape two days ago, sparking fears of a resurgence in terrorism.
Leaders from the centre-left Partido por la Democracia said the escape -- which caught the government and prison service off-guard -- reflected a lack of co-ordination between the security services.
"The break-out showed the weakness and poor performance of the intelligence aparatus," said congressman Guido Girardi.
President Eduardo Frei criticised the security services in his televised end-of-year address to the nation on Tuesday.

"Today more than ever, it is necessary to speed up our efforts to give the country a consensual, integrated, modern intelligence system ... which respects democratic authority and can be efficient," said Frei.
The men, two of whom are serving life sentences, were whisked by helicopter from a prison yard in the middle of a gun battle with prison guards.
Prison service chief Claudio Martinez resigned in disgrace soon after the jail break and calls mounted for the justice and interior ministers to step down.

The four convicts belong to the Manuel Rodriguez Patriotic Front, which fought an armed battle against General Augusto Pinochet's military government and continued to operate in the first years of democratic government in the early 1990s.
The group was involved in notorious attacks including the failed assassination attempt on Pinochet in 1986 and the murder of right-wing senator Jaime Guzman in 1991.
Police have launched a massive manhunt in the southern suburbs of Santiago and tightened controls at borders, ports and airports but no trace has yet been found of the four men.
The helicopter, which was hired from an airfield in Santiago, was found in a park in the south of the city with one of the getaway cars.
